doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Searching for a sound, reeds, and Diversatonic
summary: He is still working on his sound and reeds, objects to a Facebook post on saxophonists' height, and mentions his Diversatonic record.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Do you remember back then thinking I want to sound like whom? Did you have influences on alto and tenor or you were just finding your own way?

No, not really. You know in other words I’m still trying to figure out who I want to sound like and I’m very serious, man. I’m still — I mean I adore VanDoren reeds and I think I’ve finally solved the whole reed thing, you understand? I don’t have any more trouble with reeds on each of my instruments. I’ve got about eight reeds that sound exactly the same and they vibrate exactly the same. And nobody, it works for me and I’ve given up trying to explain to other saxophone players how to do it or whatever. You know. But sound, but not just the reed but your whole physical thing man. There’s a guy on FaceBook, he’s a very bright guy and he wrote a book about, a recent book about Johnny Hodges, you know who I’m — a recent book. I’m having a senior moment. We’re FaceBook friends and everything. But he put a post on FaceBook, and maybe his best I don’t know, he put a post on FaceBook about John Coltrane sounding taller than he was, and that Coleman Hawkins sounded taller, and certain musicians that when you saw them in person you’d be surprised at their height ‘cause they sounded so much taller. And people chimed in and they’re talking, oh yeah, so and so— and they agreed. And I’m like wait a minute. You know? Sometimes you read somebody’s — and you say well maybe I should just shut up. I had to interject and his height had nothing to do with how he sounded you know. And so again, it’s best that I don’t call names, I hope that he doesn’t hear this because he may know I’m talking about him.
Yeah, like sort of searching into another realm of fiction like.

Yeah. Yeah. It’s like — well people like to put people in boxes and they say well this group does this and this group does this. And it’s such a — at this time man, we’re into such a thing that my whole mission is to counter all that that’s going on in today’s world, you know? And I think I mentioned to you my record that I’ve got coming out is called “Diversatonic.” It addresses, because I’ve had a very diverse life. It’s not about me, it’s about society in general, and that, okay we’re all different. Get used to it. You understand? That’s what bothers me. Because we’re so confused. Our whole society is really screwed up, more so than it should be because we made progress and it seems like we’re going backwards.
